universe: GSS adults 18-44 (subgroup W: women 18-34) with a valid answer to the outcome
scope_note: Individual-level associations within the GSS. Not evidence about county or other ecological versions of these proxies, which remain unvalidated hypotheses.

tests.hypothesis: Weekly attendance adds out-of-sample discrimination for ideal 4+ children
tests.outcome: ideal number of children 4+ (CHLDIDEL 4-7 vs 0-3; 'as many as you want' excluded)
predictors: attends religious services weekly or more (ATTEND 7-8)
tests.controls: age, age squared, sex, highest degree (5 levels), Census region (4)
tests.notes: Bootstrap: PSUs resampled within strata on the test set, model held fixed (training uncertainty not propagated). Odds ratios: training fit, PSU-cluster-robust SE, stratification ignored.

tests.hypothesis: Catholic affiliation adds out-of-sample discrimination for ideal 4+ children
tests.outcome: ideal number of children 4+ (CHLDIDEL 4-7 vs 0-3; 'as many as you want' excluded)
predictors: Catholic affiliation (RELIG 2), any attendance
tests.controls: age, age squared, sex, highest degree (5 levels), Census region (4)
tests.notes: Bootstrap: PSUs resampled within strata on the test set, model held fixed (training uncertainty not propagated). Odds ratios: training fit, PSU-cluster-robust SE, stratification ignored.

tests.hypothesis: Weekly attendance adds more discrimination than Catholic affiliation (ideal 4+)
tests.outcome: ideal number of children 4+ (CHLDIDEL 4-7 vs 0-3; 'as many as you want' excluded)
predictors: attends religious services weekly or more (ATTEND 7-8)
versus
Catholic affiliation (RELIG 2), any attendance
tests.controls: age, age squared, sex, highest degree (5 levels), Census region (4)
tests.notes: auc/brier fields are the weekly-attendance model; comparator_* the Catholic-affiliation model; both fitted on the same rows. Paired bootstrap of the ΔAUC difference.
